keys12.construction: twelve canonical 381-bit residues of a uniform Fp12 element, each reduced mod the subgroup order r
keys12.scope: coordinates sampled at the tower level (a uniform Fp12 element's coordinate vector is the state distribution); NOT a pairing evaluation

high_bit_degeneracy.why: canonical residues are < r < 2^255, so a 381-bit key extraction that reads bits above 254 is degenerate (single-bin histogram). The sampler detects this BEFORE measuring uniformity and bins the 255-bit residue span instead.

degeneracy_first.verdict: no degeneration: every element has twelve distinct lanes and every lane takes (almost) all 12000 sampled values

uniformity.binning: v*4096//r: equal-probability bins over the reachable residue span [0,r)
uniformity.note: a 2^-12-class collapse would put chi2 in the 1e6 range; the observed values sit on the null mean

mulmod.implementation: four 64-bit limbs: schoolbook 4x4 product (16 mul) + Montgomery reduction (16 mul) + branch-free conditional subtraction
mulmod.object: compiled here with cc -O2, disassembled, body counted
mulmod.why_executed_equals_static: clang -O2 fully unrolls both 4-iteration loops; the disassembly contains no backward branch, so every instruction in the body executes exactly once per call
mulmod.verdict: the v32 64-Ir figure is not an implementation bound; the ledger charges the disassembled body count
